fixes.explanation: Firstfruits it is, friend. Moses says, “…take some of the firstfruits of all your produce from the soil of the land…” That's the first of the harvest going in the basket. When a tray comes out of my oven, that first cookie gets ALL the attention, so I can picture how special first-of-the-batch is.

Surplus is the extra left once everything else is counted, and that's not the word Moses uses. He says the basket gets the firstfruits of all their produce. So the first of the harvest goes in, not the pile at the end. Good thinking, friend, but the word the text gives is firstfruits.

That one sounds nice, but it isn't what the worshiper says. He never mentions vows the fathers made. He says he has entered the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to give us. So the LORD is the one who made the promise, and the worshiper is saying it came true.

That's it. The worshiper says, “…the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, toil, and oppression.” They called out, and He heard and saw. Two actions, friend, and both belong to the LORD. I think that's a comfort.

Goshen never comes up in this declaration, friend. The worshiper says the LORD heard and saw their affliction, toil, and oppression. Then he says the LORD “…brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm…” What he names is the LORD bringing them out, and that's the answer.

Haran never comes up in this declaration, friend. The worshiper says the LORD brought them to “…this place…” and gave them “…this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.” That's the destination he names. A place he never mentions can't be the answer.

Sinai never comes up in this declaration, friend. After the LORD brings them out of Egypt, the worshiper says, “And He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.” The place he names is the land the LORD gave, and that's where the basket comes from.

True, friend. Moses says, “Then you are to place the basket before the LORD your God and bow down before Him.” So the basket is set before the LORD, and then the worshiper bows down. Basket down, then bow down. I like that order.

Rejoices is right. Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household.” The word is rejoice, and the reason is the good things the LORD gave. I think that's a fine reason to smile, friend.

Foreigner is right. Moses says the rejoicing includes “…the Levite, and the foreigner dwelling among you…” So the foreigner is named right alongside the worshiper and the Levite. The text puts all three in the rejoicing.

Fasting is going without, and that isn't what this verse says, friend. Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…” The word is rejoice, in all the good things the LORD has given. Fasts doesn't fit that blank.

True. In the third year, the year of the tithe, Moses says to give it to four groups: the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. The reason he gives is that they may eat and be filled within the gates. I count four names on that list, and the tithe is for every one of them.

Moses doesn't tie this to feast days or good seasons, friend. He says, “You must be careful to follow them with all your heart and with all your soul.” The command is about how they follow, with heart and soul. Seasons never come up.

True, friend. Moses says the LORD will set Israel high above all the nations He has made, in praise, name and honor. That's three things. The verse adds that Israel will be a holy people to the LORD, as He has promised.

The text says it's true, friend. Moses says the LORD will set Israel high above all the nations He has made, in praise, name and honor. All three are in the promise. The verse also says Israel will be a holy people to the LORD, as He has promised.
